bull.b: Debt-to-equity of roughly 1%–2% across periods limits refinancing pressure and preserves balance-sheet flexibility while the pipeline is developed. This low leverage is a durable counterweight to operating losses, although it does not remove the need for funding.

Concentrating on C5a/C5aR inhibition gives InflaRx a defined scientific platform rather than unrelated projects. Vilobelimab is the lead candidate, while additional complement programs could create multiple development paths if clinical and regulatory work succeeds.

Continued research investment is necessary to advance clinical-stage assets toward regulatory milestones and potential commercialization. Regular reporting of financial condition, operations and cash flows also supports assessment of funding needs and pipeline progress over time.

bear.b: The absence of a meaningful, stable revenue base leaves InflaRx dependent on successful clinical and regulatory outcomes before operating economics can improve. Persistent gross, operating and net losses indicate profitability is not yet visible over the medium term.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means the business is not self-funding and must continue financing research and development externally. Even with some TTM improvement, recurring cash consumption can constrain execution and increase dependence on future capital access.

Material changes in shareholder equity alongside strongly negative returns on equity signal erosion from ongoing losses rather than internally generated growth. If losses continue, raising equity may be needed to sustain operations, potentially diluting existing holders.
